FollowPath.doc: Flies through a list of waypoints with the MPC's follow_path action: it passes each waypoint without stopping and settles only on the last. Waypoints are "x,y,z,yaw; x,y,z,yaw; ..." (meters, radians) in `frame`, or with roll,pitch,yaw as six values. A waypoint written "some_frame: x,y,z,yaw" is in some_frame instead, so one path can span several objects. {blackboard} references are filled in. Depth is clamped to [max_depth, min_depth] in world like PrimitiveMovePosition. Each waypoint goes to the controller in its own frame, so a path through mapping's object frames is carried along when mapping moves them (the controller resolves world and the robot's own frames once). Options after a waypoint, each "| key=value" (riptide_msgs2/PathSegment; points in the waypoint's frame), say how the path gets there: arc=cx,cy,sweep       round (cx, cy) by sweep rad (+ = counterclockwise from above) heading=path|look_at  face the direction of travel / look_at (default: blend to yaw) look_at=x,y,z         yaw_offset=rad          spin=rad (extra yaw over the leg) look_frame=frame      look_at is in this TF frame (default its origin) and the controller keeps facing it as it moves; implies heading=look_at spin_rate=rad/m       steady spin per metre (the spin_rate port sets it for every leg) yaw_frame=frame       the waypoint's roll/pitch/yaw are in this frame instead (e.g. world, to hold a world heading at a point that follows an object frame) AddWaypoint and AddArc write these.

MapConverged.doc: SUCCESS once mapping's estimate of `object` (or of every object in a comma list, "helmet,warning,pill,") is better than `target_cov`, the same error getCovariance reports. It answers immediately, so it can guard a running move in a ReactiveSequence (look around until the map has the object) and stop it the moment the estimate converges. Only estimates published after the condition started being ticked count, so one from before a SetMappingTarget reset can't pass it.

ports.name: object
ports.desc: Mapping object (mapping/<object>), or a comma list that must all converge

ports.name: target_cov
ports.desc: Converged below this error (getCovariance's)

SeenRecently.doc: SUCCESS if `object_name` was detected (at or above `min_score`) within the last `max_age_secs`. Unlike WaitForDetection it answers immediately, so it can guard a running move in a ReactiveSequence and interrupt it the moment the object comes into view. A detection mapping fused into the object counts too (mapping/fused), so a binary classifier target (bin_target1, from "fire" detections) is seen although the detector never names it.
